text: Hrafn the Squint, an older oarsman, mocks the way you pull an oar, loud enough for the whole bench to hear.

pass.text: Hrafn ends up in the bilge water. Reputation +3.

fail.text: Hrafn is stronger than he looks. Health −4, morale −5.

pass.text: You laugh. He keeps talking. Morale −2.
The steersman tells Hrafn to be quiet, and the bench calls you a tattler. Reputation −1.

text: Hrafn is telling the whole camp that you hid behind your shield in the last fight.

pass.text: On the island of hazel stakes, Hrafn yields at first blood. Reputation +6.

fail.text: Hrafn’s axe comes down on your arm, and the camp laughs. Reputation −4.

pass.text: Men who stood beside you laugh Hrafn down. Reputation +3.

fail.text: You have too few deeds to point to. The story sticks. Morale −6.

text: On the eve of battle Hrafn comes to your fire and holds out his hand. “Old quarrels are for peacetime.”

pass.text: Hrafn takes the place at your left shoulder. Morale +5.
He shrugs and walks off into the dark.

text: You wake in the dark to a hand at your purse. It is Hrafn.

pass.text: You drag him before the jarl, who fines him heavily. Reputation +4.

fail.text: He twists free and is gone with {lost} silver.

options.label: Lie still and let him go

pass.text: You keep your skin and lose {lost} silver. Morale −4.

text: In the captured town a Saxon woman named Eadgyth is binding wounds, Danish and English alike. She stitches your arm without a word.

options.label: Ask her name and come back the next day

pass.text: She lets you sit with her while she works. Morale +6.
She takes it without thanks, which seems fair. Reputation +1, morale +2.
You go back to the ship.

text: Eadgyth has no family left in her town. She asks whether a raider has room for a wife who prays to the White Christ.

pass.text: She follows the army now. Resting in camp heals you more. Morale +12.

options.label: Tell her the army is no place for her

pass.text: She nods and does not look back. Morale −4.

text: Eadgyth asks you to promise that one day you will stand at the font with her.

pass.text: She smiles for the first time in weeks. Morale +4.
She does not ask again. Morale −3.

text: Eadgyth tells you she is with child.

options.label: Swear to see the child grown

pass.text: A son is born before the next winter, and Eadgyth names him Eadric. Morale +10.

options.label: Pay a farmwife to keep them

pass.text: Mother and child stay safe behind the army. A son, Eadric, is born that winter. Silver −5, morale +3.

text: After a skirmish you stand over a wounded thegn named Wulfstan. He offers his gold ring for his life.

pass.text: His brother pays in hacksilver. Silver +12, reputation +1.
The ravens have their due. Reputation +2, morale −4.
He limps off without a word. Your bench thinks you soft. Morale +4, reputation −1.

text: A Saxon rider comes to the edge of camp under a green branch. Wulfstan sends word: if the day goes against you, come to the ford by the white stone and his men will let you through.

pass.text: You fix the white stone in your mind.

options.label: Tell the jarl Alfred is near

pass.text: The jarl nods slowly and doubles the watch. Reputation +5.

text: Halfdan is taking his men north to share out the land of Northumbria: ploughland and pasture, and no more marching.

pass.text: There is still silver in the south. Morale +2.

text: Word comes that a storm off Swanage has sunk most of the fleet that was bringing food. The camp at Exeter goes hungry.

pass.text: Thin porridge and short tempers. Morale −8, health −2.
Salt pork in the dark. Morale +4, health +4.

fail.text: You are caught with the pork and beaten. Reputation −6, health −3.

text: On Twelfth Night the army falls on Chippenham while the Saxons are at their feast. Alfred escapes into the Somerset marshes.

pass.text: Silver cups and a fine cloak. Silver +8.

options.label: Hunt for Alfred in the marsh (endurance)

pass.text: You find his trail before the rain washes it out. Reputation +4.

fail.text: Cold water to the waist and nothing to show for it. Health −4, morale −4.

text: Yule at Repton. The army feasts for twelve nights, and a boar is carried in for oaths.

pass.text: Songs, mead and a sore head. Morale +15.

options.label: Swear on the boar to kill the next champion you face

pass.text: The hall roars. Now you must keep it. Morale +8.

text: Your bench breaks into a monastery cellar full of Frankish wine.

pass.text: Morale +12, and a headache that lasts two days. Health −2.

options.label: Sell your share to a Frisian trader

pass.text: Silver +6.

text: You catch a Frankish abbot trying to slip away with his abbey’s relics.

pass.text: The monks pay to have him back. Silver +14.

options.label: Take the reliquary and let him go

pass.text: Gold and garnets. Silver +8, reputation +1.

text: Emperor Charles the Fat arrives with an army, but instead of fighting he pays the host 700 pounds of silver and lets it raid Burgundy.

options.label: Take your share and go to Burgundy

pass.text: Silver +15.

options.label: Argue for storming the city one more time

pass.text: Men respect your nerve, but the jarls take the silver. Reputation +3, morale −3.

text: A smith in a Frankish town sells blades with a name inlaid in the steel. He wants 40 silver.

pass.text: You now carry a Frankish blade. Silver −40.
You walk on.

text: Hæsten, the old sea-king, wants men to hold the fort while he takes the rest out raiding.

pass.text: Dull work, but Hæsten remembers who stayed. Reputation +4, morale −2.
A good haul from the Kentish villages. Silver +10.

fail.text: The fyrd catches you at a river crossing. Health −5.

text: The army has eaten its horses. Some men on the island are dying of hunger.

pass.text: Health −4, morale +6, reputation +2.
You stay strong, and the bench knows why. Health +3, reputation −3, morale −4.

text: News comes from the south: King Alfred is dead.

pass.text: The old men at the fire drink with you. Morale +5, reputation +1.
You think of Edington and say nothing.

text: The army winters in the abbey of Saint Bavo at Ghent. The monks fled with their saint’s bones, but they left the cellars full.

options.label: Strip the lead from the abbey roof

pass.text: It sells well to a Frisian trader, and the hall leaks all winter. Silver +8, morale −3.

options.label: Sit out the winter by the fire

pass.text: Long nights, old stories and Frankish wine. Health +5, morale +5.

text: The army is coming back from the Somme heavy with plunder when scouts report King Louis’s Franks close behind. The jarl orders the carts left by the road so the army can move faster.

pass.text: You march light and grumble every step. Morale −4.

options.label: Keep your cart and fall behind the column (endurance)

pass.text: You catch up by nightfall with your plunder. Silver +10.

fail.text: Frankish riders catch the stragglers on the road. You lose the cart and nearly your life. Health −6.

text: News comes from the Meuse: the emperor has paid Sigfred’s army more than two thousand pounds of silver to leave his lands, and given Godfrid a county in Frisia and a Frankish princess for a wife.

options.label: Say the emperor is buying his own ruin

pass.text: The bench laughs and drinks to it. Morale +4.

options.label: Go to Sigfred’s camp and ask for a share (skill)

pass.text: An old shipmate rows for Sigfred now, and he is generous. Silver +12.

fail.text: Sigfred’s men run you out of their camp. Reputation −2.

text: The jarls fill three ships with brushwood and set them alight, to drive them against the great bridge of Paris.

options.label: Pole the burning ships into the current (endurance)

pass.text: Your hands blister on the poles, but the ships reach the bridge. Reputation +4.

fail.text: The smoke and heat drive you into the river. Health −5.

pass.text: The ships run aground on the stone piers and burn out. Morale −2.

text: In the night the Seine floods and sweeps away the smaller bridge. Twelve Frankish warriors are cut off in its tower on the south bank.

options.label: Join the attack on the tower (strength)

pass.text: The tower burns, and the defenders come out fighting. Reputation +4, silver +4.

fail.text: A stone from the top of the tower catches your helmet. Health −5.

options.label: Argue that the twelve be offered their lives

pass.text: Nobody listens, but you sleep better than the men who took the tower. Morale +3, reputation −1.

text: The harvest has failed across Francia. Horses die in the fields, and the army’s stores run low.

options.label: Share your food with your crew

pass.text: They will remember it. Health −3, morale +3, reputation +2.

options.label: Buy grain from a Frisian trader (8 silver)

pass.text: Bread, at a robber’s price. Health +4, morale +2.
Hunger gnaws at you. Morale −5.

text: The army’s camp on the Dyle sits in a bend of the river, with marsh on two sides. The jarls want a ditch dug across the dry ground.

pass.text: By dawn the ditch is chest-deep, and the jarl sees whose spade it was. Reputation +3.

fail.text: You are asleep on your spade by midnight, and the steersman tells everyone. Reputation −1, morale −2.

pass.text: You rest instead. Health +4.

text: Back in England, the fleet rows up from the coast of Kent and finds a half-built English fort in the marsh. Its builders have fled.

options.label: Finish the rampart and make it yours (endurance)

pass.text: Your part of the wall is the best in camp. Reputation +3.

fail.text: A timber slips and crushes your foot. Health −4.

options.label: Raid the farms of the Weald

pass.text: Kentish pigs and a silver brooch. Silver +6.

fail.text: The Kentish fyrd is waiting at the ford. Health −5.

text: When the English took the fort at Benfleet, they took Hæsten’s wife and two sons with it. Now King Alfred has sent all three back unharmed: one boy is his godson, the other is godson to Ealdorman Æthelred.

options.label: Call it the act of a fool

pass.text: The bench laughs. Morale +3.

options.label: Call it the act of a king who keeps his word

pass.text: A few of the older men nod. Morale +1, reputation +1.

text: Trapped on the island at Buttington, the jarls mean to break out across the river at first light. Someone has to lead the rush into the English shields.

pass.text: You are first across, and the army follows your shield. Reputation +6.

fail.text: You are first across, and the English are ready for you. Health −7.

pass.text: Another man leads the rush.

text: The army shelters inside the old Roman walls of Chester, empty for centuries. The English burn the fields around it and drive the cattle away.

pass.text: Geese and a deer: your crew eats tonight. Morale +5.

fail.text: An English patrol chases you back to the walls. Health −4.

pass.text: Under a fallen roof you find a jar of old coins. Silver +9.

fail.text: Only rubble and nettles.

text: King Alfred’s men are building two forts on the Lea below your ships. If they finish them, the ships will never reach the sea again.

options.label: Burn their timber in the night (skill)

pass.text: The timber burns, and the work stops for a week. Reputation +5.

fail.text: The sentries are awake. Health −5.

options.label: Get ready to leave the ships and march overland

pass.text: Leaving the ships for the Londoners to take hurts. Morale −4.

text: Your son Eadric is nearly grown, and he has been practising with a spear behind the tents. He asks to come to the shield-wall with you.

options.label: Let him carry your spare shield behind the wall

pass.text: He stays behind the line and watches every blow. Morale +6.

options.label: Send him home to his mother

pass.text: He goes, angry, and you are glad of it. Morale +3.

options.label: Give him a place in the wall beside you

pass.text: Eadric takes his place at your shoulder, white-faced and steady. Morale +4.

text: Æthelwold, King Alfred’s nephew, has come to York with a claim to the throne of Wessex. He promises the Danes plunder if they help him take it.

pass.text: He gives you a gold ring from his own hand. Silver +6, reputation +2.

options.label: Say no West Saxon will ever be king of the Danes

pass.text: Half the hall agrees with you. Morale +3.

text: A young skald from Iceland wants to hear about Ashdown and Edington from a man who stood there.

pass.text: He listens to every word. Reputation +3.

options.label: Tell it better than it happened (skill)

pass.text: By the end of the night the whole hall is listening. Reputation +5.

fail.text: An old man who was at Ashdown corrects you in front of everyone. Reputation −2.

text: A young raider calls you grandfather in front of the whole bench.

pass.text: He won’t say it again. Reputation +3.

fail.text: He is quicker than you were at his age. Health −3, morale −4.

options.label: Laugh and tell him about Ashdown

pass.text: The young ones listen. Morale +4.

text: A drinking-horn argument turns into a brawl in the hall.

pass.text: You flatten a loudmouth. Reputation +3.

fail.text: You meet a bench with your face. Health −4.

pass.text: The jarl’s men note your calm. Reputation +1.
You drink alone. Morale −3.

text: A skald offers to put your name into a verse, for a price.

pass.text: Your name will be sung at the fires. Reputation +4.
Your boast rings true. Reputation +3.

fail.text: They laugh at you. Morale −6.

text: A shipmate burns with fever and has nothing to eat.

pass.text: He lives, and the crew respects you for it. Morale +8, health −2.
Nobody speaks to you tonight. Morale −5, reputation −1.

text: Your bench drags a frightened monk out of a church. He swears the silver is buried under the altar.

pass.text: Ten silver in your purse, and a cold feeling. Silver +10, morale −5.
Word of your mercy travels. Reputation +2.

text: The salted fish on the ship has gone bad.

pass.text: Your stomach holds.

fail.text: You retch for a day. Health −6.

pass.text: Hunger gnaws at you. Morale −6.

text: A grey-bearded raider offers to teach you a trick with the shield.

pass.text: You learn to read a man’s feet. Skill +1.
You hold your own. Strength +1.

fail.text: He knocks you flat. Health −5.

text: Men are playing hnefatafl for silver by the fire.

pass.text: Your king escapes to the corner. Silver +4.

fail.text: Your king is surrounded. Silver −4.

pass.text: A good game to watch. Morale +2.

text: The enemy’s horses are picketed just past the river, lightly guarded.

pass.text: You sell them to the jarl’s stablemaster. Silver +8, reputation +1.

fail.text: A guard’s spear catches your leg. Health −5.

pass.text: You leave them.

text: The bear-shirts invite you to their rite around a great fire.

pass.text: You howl until dawn and wake with burns. Morale +10, health −3.
You watch from the dark.

text: A seeress throws rune-staves for anyone with silver.

pass.text: She sees ravens over your enemies. Morale +8, {god}’s favour +1.

fail.text: She will not say what she saw. Morale −6.

pass.text: You walk past.

text: A hard frost. {crewFirst} has lost his cloak.

pass.text: Two men under one cloak. Morale +4, health −3.
You sleep warm but badly. Morale −3.

text: A local boy darts off with a loaf from your pack.

pass.text: You get the bread back. He runs off crying.

fail.text: He is faster than you. Morale −2.

pass.text: You had a brother that age. Morale +3.

text: Three men from your bench plan to slip away tonight. They ask you to come.

pass.text: They are caught at dawn. Reputation +4, morale −4.
You turn over and say nothing.

text: The camp holds glíma wrestling, with an arm-ring for the winner.

pass.text: You throw three men. Reputation +3, silver +3.

fail.text: You are thrown in the first bout. Health −2, morale −2.

pass.text: Morale +2.

text: The locals avoid an old burial mound. They say a dead king lies inside with his gold.

pass.text: Old gold, green with age. Silver +10.

fail.text: Something moves in the dark of the mound, and you run. Morale −10.

pass.text: You leave the dead alone.

text: The church has silver plate. The priest begs you to leave the altar cross.

pass.text: Silver +9, morale −2.
Silver +5, reputation +1.

text: A trader from Dublin offers a ring-sword for 14 silver. That is very cheap.

pass.text: It is the real thing. You now carry a ring-sword.

fail.text: It snaps at the first test. The trader has already gone.

pass.text: You let him go.

text: Ivar the Boneless’s hearth-men walk the lines, picking men for a dangerous scouting ride.

pass.text: You bring back word of the enemy’s camp. Reputation +5, silver +4.

fail.text: You are spotted and ridden down. Health −5.

pass.text: You stay where you are.

text: The ale has run out and tempers are short.

options.label: Buy from a local alewife (2 silver)

pass.text: Silver −2, morale +10.
Morale −4.

text: Men spit when you pass. Nobody wants a níðingr at their fire.

pass.text: Morale −6.

options.label: Buy a round of ale (4 silver)

pass.text: A few men drink with you. Silver −4, reputation +2.

text: A green recruit, Ulf the Young, asks you to teach him how to stand in the wall.

options.label: Teach him and take him on your side

pass.text: Ulf joins your part of the wall. Reputation +2.
He finds another teacher.

text: Two men of your crew quarrel over a dead man’s shield. They want their captain to judge.

pass.text: Reputation +2.
The crew enjoys it more than either man. Morale +4.
Silver +3, reputation −2.
